<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 2 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 2 ==

== Biography ==

Jack Pumpkinhead, also called Jack or Pumpkinhead, is a man built from wood and topped with a carved pumpkin for a head. He was fashioned by Tip, who afterward maintained that "Jack belongs to me, for I made him even if the old witch did bring him to life" — the witch in question being old Mombi, who animated him by means of a magical powder kept in an old pepper-box. He received his name when a companion declared, "I believe I will name the fellow 'Jack Pumpkinhead!'"

Jack's body is stiff and poorly suited to ordinary movement. His joints are weak, and when he first tried to walk he had to be dragged and pushed into motion, tumbling several times before he could manage the bend in the road on his own. Sitting is especially hazardous to him: on one occasion he attempted to rest on an old sawhorse, and as soon as he bent his joints further than usual they gave way entirely, sending him crashing to the ground. After this he was advised, "I guess you'd better remain standing, hereafter. It seems the safest way."

Jack does not share ordinary human needs. When invited to breakfast, he declined to join in, explaining, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are."

On the road to the Emerald City, Jack presented himself to the Guardian of the Gates, who asked who he was and what his business might be. Jack answered plainly, "My name is Jack Pumpkinhead, but as to my business, I haven't the least idea in the world what it is," an answer that left the Guardian visibly dissatisfied.

At a river crossing, a ferryman refused passage and dismissed him as a "pumpkinheaded loon," indifferent to whether he sank or swam. Undisturbed, Jack replied, "Don't worry about me, I'm sure I ought to float beautifully," and waded in himself, holding the tail of the Saw-Horse to keep his pumpkin head above the water while the party crossed.

== Narrative role ==

Jack Pumpkinhead — also known simply as Jack or Pumpkinhead — began his existence as a carved wooden figure fashioned by Tip. After building the body and fitting it with a pumpkin head, Tip dressed the finished figure in clothes taken from Old Mombi's chest and gave it the name "Jack Pumpkinhead."

As Jack and Tip set out together, Jack grew anxious that his wooden joints would wear out from walking. When he attempted to sit down on an old sawhorse resting at the edge of a wood, his joints gave way entirely and he collapsed; Tip lifted him back to his feet and advised him to remain standing from then on. The pair debated whether the sawhorse truly resembled a real horse, weighing its tree-trunk body, branch tail, knot eyes, and carved mouth, and Jack observed that since he himself was made of wood yet alive, the sawhorse might likewise be brought to life.

In the Emerald City, Jack admitted his mistake in assuming that an interpreter would be needed. The Scarecrow then declared the two of them friends and led Jack off to play quoits. Jack Pumpkinhead's meeting with His Majesty the Scarecrow, ruler of the Emerald City, is also recorded, along with a shared discovery that only one language was spoken throughout Oz.

Later, while crossing a river, Jack's pumpkin head was swept downstream; Tip retrieved it with a long pole and reattached it to his neck, after which Jack worried anxiously that water or sunshine might spoil or crack it. The group then remounted the Saw-Horse and resumed traveling toward Nick Chopper, with Jack and the horse bickering along the way. Upon arrival, Nick Chopper welcomed Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and explained that the engraved star on his chest covered the patch where the Wizard of Oz had placed his heart.

The group later escaped a field of sunflowers by riding forward with their eyes closed, following the lead of the Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse. Afterward, Nick Chopper amputated Jack's damaged left leg and fitted it to the Saw-Horse, an exchange that prompted further bickering between Jack and the horse before the group resumed its travel toward the Emerald City.

Nick Chopper subsequently repaired Jack's broken leg with a table leg, and the group dispersed to gather materials for an aerial machine; palm leaves were fastened as wings, and Jack's broom was added as a tail for steering. The finished craft, the Gump, then flew south carrying Tip, the Scarecrow, Nick Chopper, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Woggle-Bug, and the Saw-Horse aboard.

== Personality ==

Jack shows an amiable, unguarded temperament, meeting even his own uncertain nature with equanimity rather than distress: asked by the Guardian of the Gates about his business, he answers, smilingly, that he has "not the least idea in the world what it is," untroubled by not knowing. The same good humor surfaces when a hostile ferryman dismisses him outright — Jack answers with a smile that he expects to "float beautifully," an unshaken cheerfulness even when others treat him with contempt or indifference.

His curiosity runs outward more than inward: he watches Tip "curiously" over breakfast, remarking only that he is "not made the same way" rather than pressing the matter, and later offers Tip the practical suggestion of carving ears for the Saw-Horse so it might be told what to do — a small but concrete instance of problem-solving. Beneath this composure runs a current of physical anxiety tied to his fragile condition: he asks, fearfully, whether fire is dangerous to pumpkins, a rare admission of worry set against his usual even temper.

== Appearance ==

Jack Pumpkinhead is built with a carved pumpkin for a head, the detail behind the name given him at his creation. His frame is heavy and awkward to move, needing to be dragged and walked into position by bending one leg's joints, then the other, while being pushed from behind.

His joints are notably weak: bending them further than usual makes them give way entirely, and he comes clattering to the ground, after which his arms and legs must be straightened and his head checked for cracks. Because of this fragility, remaining standing rather than sitting is judged the safer posture for him. When wading through water, he must keep his pumpkin head lifted above the surface to keep it from harm.

== Powers ==

Jack Pumpkinhead owes his very existence to magic: he was carved from wood and a pumpkin, then brought to life by a magical powder kept in an old pepper-box. This origin leaves him fundamentally unlike an ordinary person — he does not eat, telling Tip plainly, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are," and declining to join him at breakfast.

His wooden, jointed frame is both a strength and a liability. The joints allow him to walk and stand once set in motion, but they are weak and prone to giving way entirely under strain, as when he tried to sit and collapsed in a clattering heap. When faced with crossing a river, Jack showed no fear of the water, confidently telling the ferryman, "I'm sure I ought to float beautifully" — a buoyancy his pumpkin-and-wood body would be expected to have, though only he voiced this expectation.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Tip]]''' — family. Tip carved Jack Pumpkinhead's body and brought him to life with the Powder of Life, later insisting "Jack belongs to me, for I made him even if the old witch did bring him to life"; the bond seems to carry an almost paternal weight, as Jack is said to have addressed Tip as "dear father."

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — acquaintance. In the Tin Woodman's company, Jack seems to have been accepted as a kindred figure, told "you are certainly unusual, and therefore worthy to become a member of our select society," suggesting an easy welcome among fellow unusual beings.

'''[[Saw-Horse]]''' — friendly_rivalry. Their bond seems built more on shared mishap than rivalry: after wading and swimming together across a river, the Saw-Horse remarked "I didn't mind swimming, at all," to which Jack answered, "Nor did I."

'''[[The Scarecrow]]''' — friend. Their rapport appears to rest on a mutual understanding of what it means to be a made, not born, creature, captured in an exchange noting "there is this difference between us, that whereas I will bend, but not break, you will break, but not bend."

'''[[Woggle-Bug]]''' — acquaintance. Their exchanges suggest quiet agreement rather than closeness, as when Jack simply acknowledged, "That is true."

== Trivia ==

* The name "Jack Pumpkinhead" was chosen for him on the spot by his creator, who settled on it "after a moment's thought."
* He does not eat: when invited to share a meal, he explained, "I don't seem to be made the same way you are."
* It was Jack's own idea to fashion ears for the newly animated Saw-Horse, reasoning that ears would let it be told what to do.
* Facing a river crossing with no boat available, he showed no fear of sinking, remarking that he was sure he "ought to float beautifully."

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 5 ==

== Biography ==

Jack Pumpkinhead, also known simply as Jack, is associated with a private graveyard, described as such by the Tin Woodman when Dorothy comes upon it. The graveyard holds tombstones marking not death but recurring spoilage: one reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled April 9th," a second reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled October 2nd," and a third reads "Here Lies the Mortal Part of JACK PUMPKINHEAD Which Spoiled January 24th."

The existence of these markers puzzles Dorothy, who remarks that she thought nobody ever died in Oz — a reaction that underscores how unusual it is for Jack to have a graveyard of his own despite still being present and, as the tombstones themselves show, having outlasted each recorded spoiling of his "mortal part."

== Narrative role ==

Jack Pumpkinhead is first encountered when Dorothy and her companions stop at his pumpkin farm along the road, where Nick Chopper, the Tin Woodman, recounts the story of the Powder of Life that had first brought Jack to life. During the visit, Dorothy comes upon a small graveyard on the property and asks what it is; the Tin Woodman explains it is Jack Pumpkinhead's own private graveyard. Puzzled, since she believed no one ever died in Oz, Dorothy reads the tombstones herself. Each one marks not a death but a spoiling: one records that the mortal part of Jack Pumpkinhead spoiled on April 9th, a second on October 2nd, and a third on January 24th, showing that Jack has already gone through several pumpkin heads before the one he currently wears.

== Personality ==

Jack Pumpkinhead's face is described as jolly and smiling, a bearing that drew Button-Bright to grow fond of him.

The Tin Woodman's readiness to fetch Dorothy to Jack's house upon learning he is "still alive" suggests Jack is held in genuine affection by his companions, despite the fragile, ever-spoiling nature of his pumpkin head.

== Appearance ==

Jack Pumpkinhead's defining physical trait is named directly: his head is carved from a pumpkin, and this head constitutes what is called his "mortal part." This mortal part decays over time — tombstones in his private graveyard record that it "spoiled" on three separate occasions, dated April 9th, October 2nd, and January 24th, indicating that his pumpkin head has been replaced more than once.

== Powers ==

Jack Pumpkinhead does not perish in the ordinary sense. Behind his home lies a private graveyard holding no bodies, only small tombstones marking when a previous pumpkin head "spoiled" — first on April 9th, then October 2nd, then January 24th. Since nobody is ever said to truly die in Oz, this suggests that the spoiling of a pumpkin head ends only that "mortal part" of Jack rather than Jack himself, hinting at a capacity to continue on beyond the loss of any single head.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. Their bond seems close, as Dorothy sighs "Poor Jack! I'm sorry he had to die in three parts," suggesting genuine concern for Jack's periodic spoiling.

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — friend. The Tin Woodman's declaration, "So you shall, since he is still alive. Come with me to his house," suggests a welcoming, supportive bond toward Jack.

'''[[Ozma]]''' — family. Jack's own words, "Ozma's my parent, you know, because she built my body and carved my pumpkin head," suggest he regards her as a parental figure owing to her role in his creation.

'''[[Button-Bright]]''' — friend. The boy's fondness seems to stem from Jack's demeanor, as "Jack's face was so jolly and smiling that the boy soon grew to like him."

== Trivia ==

* Jack Pumpkinhead maintains a private graveyard containing the remains of his previous pumpkin heads once they spoiled.
* Three graves are recorded there, marking heads that spoiled on April 9th, October 2nd, and January 24th.
* Dorothy initially believed nobody in Oz ever died, making the discovery of Jack's graveyard a surprise to her.
* Despite the graves marking his spoiled heads, Jack Pumpkinhead is still alive, as Nick Chopper confirms when referring to him as "still alive."

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* Along the road they visit Jack Pumpkinhead at his pumpkin farm and hear the Tin Woodman's account of the Powder of Life.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 6 ==

== Biography ==

Jack Pumpkinhead is a farmer whose farm consists of a vast pumpkin field, where some of the pumpkins grow to enormous size. He designed his own house, which stands not far from the Scarecrow's mansion. Like the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Tiktok, he has no need to sleep. He counts the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow among his companions, and, together with the Tin Woodman and the Shaggy Man, he declared his intention to stand by Ozma.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — friend. Jack Pumpkinhead is named alongside the Scarecrow as one of the Wizard's old friends, and the two are described waiting out a night together at the Forbidden Fountain, suggesting a close bond.

'''[[Ozma]]''' — friend. Jack Pumpkinhead's declaration that he would stand by Ozma suggests loyalty toward her.

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — friend. His presence alongside the Tin Woodman during a visit to the tin castle suggests a friendly acquaintance.

'''[[Tiktok]]''' — friend. His overnight vigil beside the Forbidden Fountain alongside Tiktok suggests a companionable relationship.

=== Events ===

* The group decides to rest, eat supper, and continue their journey the next day, planning to visit the Rigmaroles and Flutterbudgets before calling on the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Scarecrow.
* The group visits the Scarecrow's new corn-shaped mansion and Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin farm; both agree to join them in the Emerald City to support Ozma.
</div>
